sections.html:
Clark County is in southern Indiana on the north bank of the Ohio River, directly across from Louisville, Kentucky. Jeffersonville is the county seat and largest city. Clarksville, Charlestown, Sellersburg, Henryville, Marysville and Speed also appear on deeds. The 2020 census counted 121,093 people in the county and 49,447 in Jeffersonville, much of that growth from annexation.

Because of that annexation, tax districts vary across city limits. Check which taxing district your parcel falls in, since the bill combines county, municipal and school levies.

River flooding and tornadoes are part of local history. The March 2012 outbreak heavily damaged Marysville and Henryville, so a home there may have been rebuilt or repaired, and a buyer's inspector will ask for permits and repair records. If your house sits near the river or a creek, ask your insurer about flood coverage and keep any elevation or damage paperwork.

Clark County taxes are paid to the county treasurer in two installments, generally due May 10 and November 10, with paper bills mailed in early April. Copy A of the bill is paid in the spring and Copy B in the fall. When a due date falls on a weekend, the state calendar moves it to the next business day.

The treasurer's office is at 300 Corporate Drive, Suite 105, Jeffersonville, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed from noon to 1 p.m. The phone number is 812-285-6205. Mailed payments go to PO Box 1689, Evansville, IN 47706, and you should include Copy A or Copy B of the bill and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for a receipt.

Several local banks accept payment during collection season, but only with the bill in hand, only for accounts with no delinquency, and only by the due date.

Indiana's deadline for a Form 130 appeal is June 15 of the year the county sends the assessment notice, or of the year the tax bill is mailed when no Form 11 is sent. File one petition per parcel with the assessing official, and check your own notice for the exact date.

After filing, the assessor schedules an informal meeting and reports the result to the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals. The board must hold its hearing within 180 days of the petition, with at least 30 days of mailed notice. A $50 penalty can apply if you skip the hearing without a valid continuance or withdrawal. If you disagree with the board, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

Bring evidence to the informal meeting: recent sales of similar houses nearby, an appraisal, or photos of damage and needed repairs. A value that reflects the house's real condition is easier to win when the paperwork is organized.

sections.h2: How a Clark County tax sale works
sections.html:
Real property with delinquent taxes is offered at a tax certificate sale run by the Clark County Treasurer. A winning bidder receives a lien through a Tax Sale Certificate issued by the County Auditor.

The owner has one year from the sale date to redeem the property by paying the amounts set by Indiana Code, including interest. If it is not redeemed, the bidder may seek a tax deed. Property listings are published at sriservices.com, and a bidder should get legal advice.

The late penalty before that stage is 5% of the delinquent tax if you pay within 30 days and have no earlier delinquency, and 10% otherwise. If you own a house heading toward the sale list, selling first can keep the amount from growing.

Clark County sellers often face deferred repairs, inherited houses and landlord exits, and each of these carries tax questions. Here is a short checklist.

  • Request the current balance from the treasurer before choosing a closing date.
  • Complete the sales disclosure form, which Indiana requires before the deed reaches the county auditor.
  • Gather permits and storm repair records if the home is near the river or in a tornado-hit area.
  • If you claim the homestead deduction, a buyer who purchases after the assessment date can claim it by December 31 of the purchase year.

Back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so they do not block a sale. A cash offer for a Clark County house can close without repairs or showings, and the title company settles taxes from the proceeds.

Before the closing date, get the payoff from the treasurer in writing and hand it to the title company. If the bill has gone past a due date, the penalty is 5% or 10%, and it grows with each missed installment, so a quick closing usually costs less than a long listing period.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Generally May 10 and November 10. Copy A of the bill is paid in the spring and Copy B in the fall, and bills usually go out in early April.

faqs.q: Where is the Clark County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: At 300 Corporate Drive, Suite 105, Jeffersonville, IN 47130, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It closes from noon to 1 p.m. Mail goes to PO Box 1689, Evansville, IN 47706.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Clark County tax sale property?
faqs.a: One year from the sale date. After that the bidder may seek a tax deed under Indiana Code, and redemption requires paying the amounts the statute sets, including interest.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Clark County?
faqs.a: June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed, using Form 130. File one petition per parcel and check your Form 11 for the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clark County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure first, because penalties of 5% or 10% may apply.
